crates.title: CR/LF/CRLF normalization for finite character lists (adapted source)
crates.limitations: The original crates.io source is retained unchanged, but its character-pattern switches are unsupported by the pinned Aeneas translator. The three guard replacements have a Kani-checked one-step equivalence under the documented two-reply, non-panicking callback model. This is not a generic contextual-equivalence proof for every Rust Iterator implementation, nor a direct Aeneas proof of the unmodified release. The end-to-end Aeneas guarantee remains scoped to the adapted extraction and total fused list iterator model. Arbitrary external iterators, their panics or divergence, and iterators that resume after None are outside the end-to-end theorem. No separate general memory-safety claim is made.

crates.title: Exact next-word output and state update in XorShiftRng
crates.limitations: The result covers only try_next_u32 on x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu without serde. Seed construction, next_u64, fill_bytes, external-RNG initialization, formatting, inherited Rng wrappers, and serde are not verified. The all-zero state is included; no seed invariant, nonzero-state invariant, period, distribution, or cryptographic property is established. The three standard-operator models are executable definitions with Kani correspondence evidence, rather than body-proved translations of the original std implementations. Kani uses a different Rust nightly from extraction, so its correspondence checks are not direct proofs of that extraction toolchain's std bodies.
